# Important Globals {#important-globals}

## Spacing {#spacing}

When considering margins and padding, column sizes, image widths, etc., keep numbers to multiples of 8\. This way it matches the styles used in the core stylesheet and Figma. We use multiples of 8 because it scales nicely between screen sizes (screen resolutions are generally a multiple of 8, and half-pixels are blurry). 

Quick ref:  
8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64, 72, 80, 88, 96, 104, 112, 120, 128, 136, 144, 152, 160

## Font sizes {#font-sizes}

Default font sizes are as follows:

Paragraph: 16px

Lead paragraph: 22px

Intro paragraph: 30px

Small: 14px

H1: 50px

H2: 34px

H3: 30px

H4: 26px

H5: 22px

H6: 18px

## 

## URL and page title formatting {#url-and-page-title-formatting}

To keep page titles consistent between pages, use the following format:

**Page Title | Sub Category if Applicable | Title of the Website**

Write the title of the website out in full, e.g. Linewize New Zealand as opposed to Linewize NZ.

To make URLs easy to understand by search engines, use dashes between words and make sure the structure of the URL matches the structure of the navigation:

**linewize.com/sub-category-if-applicable/page-title**

# Choosing a template {#choosing-a-template}

There is a default set of templates for each region. The set includes:

* Webpage  
* Webpage with CTA  
* Landing Page  
* Landing Page with CTA

Webpage is the standard base template for all pages that don’t have the Let’s Connect section at the bottom.

Webpage with CTA includes a global Let’s Connect section. If your page includes a Let’s Connect section at the bottom, use this template to allow global updates to the Let’s Connect section to propagate.

Landing Page is the same as the webpage template except it uses minimal navigation in the header. Use this for campaign landing pages that are separate from the general site.

Landing Page with CTA is the same as the landing page template except it has the Let’s Connect section at the bottom.

Find the correct template for your page by finding the template named with the format “\[Brand\] \[Region if applicable\] \[WP(Webpage)/LP(Landing page)\] \[With CTA if applicable\]”. For example, the Linewize Australia webpage template is named “Linewize AU WP”, and the Linewize US landing page with CTA template is named “Linewize US LP with CTA”.

## Custom section guidelines {#custom-section-guidelines}

In general, when creating a new custom section, settings should be as follows:

Content alignment: Center content;

Max width: 1280px;

Padding: 

* Desktop:  
  * Top/Bottom: 64px or 4rem  
  * Left/Right: 16px or 1rem  
* Mobile:  
  * Top/Bottom: 32px or 2rem  
  * Left/Right: 16px or 1rem

A single “rem” is equal to the base font size of the user’s browser. By default, on most browsers, this is equal to 16px. It can be used to make things responsive, since some smaller devices have smaller “rems”.

## Exceptions {#exceptions}

When two sections have the same background colour, you probably want the top/bottom padding to be half of the recommended or less. 

When the section includes a carousel, you may want more Left/Right padding to make space for the Next/Previous arrows. 

## Saving Sections {#saving-sections}

Sometimes you’ve created a custom section that you’d like to copy to another page. You can save a section in the Hubspot instance and reuse it elsewhere.

To save a section, hover over it until the options pop up over the top left of the section, then open the dropdown menu and click “Save section”.

![][image5]

That section will then appear under the Saved section of the Sections tab of the Add pane:

![][image6]

## Advanced form styling {#advanced-form-styling}

For advanced form embedding, e.g. for embedding a form within a rich text field, or nested in a pullout, or any other scenario where using the Form module is impractical, you’ll need to use the form’s embed code and style it with CSS classes.

[HubSpot documentation on the form embed code](https://legacydocs.hubspot.com/docs/methods/forms/advanced_form_options)

For example, the NZ Book a demo form code, when copied, is:

| \<script charset="utf-8" type="text/javascript" src="//js.hsforms.net/forms/embed/v2.js"\>\</script\> \<script\>   hbspt.forms.create({     region: "na1",     portalId: "7977292",     formId: "ff1b5be8-9298-4acb-bd67-b9d702a299e3"   }); \</script\> |
| :---- |

To add a CSS class to the form, add the cssClass line **(note the added “,” to the end of the previous line)**:

| \<script charset="utf-8" type="text/javascript" src="//js.hsforms.net/forms/embed/v2.js"\>\</script\> \<script\>   hbspt.forms.create({     region: "na1",     portalId: "7977292",     formId: "ff1b5be8-9298-4acb-bd67-b9d702a299e3",     cssClass: "form-underline"   }); \</script\> |
| :---- |

# Navigation menus {#navigation-menus}

Navigation menus are managed in the HubSpot website navigation settings. 

[Hubspot Knowledge Base article for navigation menus](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/website-pages/set-up-your-site-s-navigation-menus)

Each regional site has two navigation menus \- one for the top nav, seen on every page, and another more comprehensive navigation used for the site map page.

The global header section includes a breakpoint option. This dictates the screen size at which the navigation collapses into a hamburger menu. If the menu is looking a bit cramped at a particular screen size, either remove some items from the menu or select a larger breakpoint.

The global header section allows switching between a megamenu-style of menu and a basic dropdown style. When megamenu is selected, additional options will become available allowing you to create small descriptions for primary menu items.

# Using CSS classes {#using-css-classes}

CSS classes are a more advanced way to manage the styling of elements. The HubSpot Blog has a good article on how CSS classes work, and how to apply them to elements, [here](https://blog.hubspot.com/website/what-is-css-class).

All the CSS classes for Qoria styling have already been created using a customised version of the [Bootstrap](https://getbootstrap.com/docs/5.3/getting-started/introduction/) toolkit as the base for the classes.

## 

## Customising text {#customising-text}

Add the following classes to text to apply the corresponding styling:

| Colours .text-primary .text-secondary .text-red .text-orange .text-blue .text-dark .text-light .text-white .text-reset \- removes the element’s style colour and adopts the *parent’s* style colour. | Weights .fw-light .fw-regular .fw-semibold .fw-bold |
| :---- | :---- |
|  | Line heights .lh-1 \- single line-spacing .lh-sm \- smaller line-spacing .lh-base \- standard/default .lh-lg \- larger line-spacing  |
| Decoration .text-decoration-underline ~~.text-decoration-line-through~~ .text-decoration-none | Font sizes .fs-1 .fs-2 .fs-3 .fs-4 .fs-5 .fs-6 |
| Italics *.fst-italic* .fst-normal \- removes italics from the element. |  |

## Using classes to reset link styling {#using-classes-to-reset-link-styling}

By default, links are Qoria teal. To reset the colour change and make the link adopt its parent’s text colour, use the class “text-reset”.

# Responsive padding and margins {#responsive-padding-and-margins}

There are two ways to create responsive padding and margins in the current system. 

## HubSpot {#hubspot}

HubSpot allows each section, column, and row in their drag-and-drop templates to have padding and margins set for desktop and mobile. This is the most user-friendly way to manage padding and margin, but it is limited in a couple of ways \- you can’t set “in-between” size settings, and it can’t be used for elements within modules.

Toggle between desktop and mobile settings with these buttons:

![][image10]

## Bootstrap {#bootstrap}

A more advanced method to manage padding and margin is with the pre-coded Bootstrap padding and margin classes. See the [section on CSS classes](#using-css-classes) to find out how to use them. The downside to this method is it can’t be used for HubSpot Sections, Rows or Columns, only where it’s possible to add classes.

Read [this section](https://getbootstrap.com/docs/5.3/utilities/spacing/) of documentation on Bootstrap padding and margins for information on what classes to use \- you can use different classes to apply different padding or margins at different screen widths. 

This table shows the values assigned to each number of the Bootstrap padding and margin classes:

| Number | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| 0 | 0 |
| 1 | .25rem |
| 2 | .5rem |
| 3 | 1rem |
| 4 | 1.5rem |
| 5 | 2rem |
| 6 | 3rem |
| 7 | 3.75rem |
| 8 | 4.5rem |

For example, a class of “p-md-6” would assign a padding (p) value of 3rem (6 in the table) when the screen hits medium (md) width or wider.

# Adjusting layout {#adjusting-layout}

## Use spacers instead of left/right padding {#use-spacers-instead-of-left/right-padding}

If a section is too wide for the content (for example, a section of text that is full-width), avoid using left and right padding to squish in the edges of the text. It might look okay at large screen sizes, but at smaller screen sizes (e.g. tablets) the padding remains the same, leading to a far-too-narrow paragraph. Use a horizontal spacer module on either side of the text module to bring in the edges \- spacer modules are responsive at all sizes.

![][image11]

A text section with 200px added as left/right padding

![][image12]

Same section viewed on a tablet-sized screen \- it’s far too narrow

![][image13]

A text section with a horizontal spacer added on either side \- the horizontal spacers are two columns wide each.

![][image14]  
Same section viewed on a tablet-sized screen \- more in proportion.

## Avoid negative margins (unless overlapping content) {#avoid-negative-margins-(unless-overlapping-content)}

Avoid using negative margins where possible \- they can easily break a responsive design when used inappropriately. Try reducing the padding of other elements if you want to reduce spacing.

Sometimes a design calls for one section to have content that overlaps another section, e.g. the “What is Linewize Connect?” section overlaps the “Why a single platform?” section.

Use negative margins to get this sort of layout to work. On the Linewize Connect section, the grey section has had its bottom padding set to “0”. The white section has had extra top padding added, and set to “9rem”, while the top margin is set to “-5rem”. This means the white section overlaps the grey section by 5rem, giving 4rem of space between the bottom of the “What is Linewize Connect?” box and the top of the next heading. 

![][image15]

# Sending pages from Content Staging to Live {#sending-pages-from-content-staging-to-live}

1. Navigate to the Content Staging section of the AU HubSpot.   
   1. Marketing \> Website \> Website Pages.  
   2. More Tools \> Content Staging.  
2. Change view from Manage to Publish:  
   ![][image16]  
3. Click Publish All to Live Domain (top right).

Note: Resolve URL conflicts by unpublishing the *currently live* pages before publishing the pages that are set to replace them.

# Modules {#modules-1}

## HubDB Cards {#hubdb-cards}

The HubDB Cards modules use a HubDB spreadsheet to control their contents. We usually use them when we require filtering of cards.

### Fields {#fields}

**Selection (Manual or Automatic):** Manual means you will be manually selecting each row from the spreadsheet to include in the cards. Automatic lets the system decide based on settings you apply.

**Source Table:** Where you select the HubDB to use for content.

**Filters:** Where you can filter which rows are included based on values in a column. Multiple filters can be created.

**Filter Property:** Which column to filter by. Use the column ID, not the label.

**Filter Value:** The value to look for when matching rows.

**Filter Operator:** How the value is applied to the column when selecting rows. For information on how these operators work, check out the [HubSpot documentation](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/guides/api/cms/hubdb#filter-returned-rows).

**Order by:** Which column to use when ordering content. Use the column ID, not the label. 

**Reverse Order:** Reverses the ordering specified in the previous field.

**Sub-filter options:** These are the filters which appear on the page. For each sub-filter, select the column whose values you want to be able to filter by. Multiple filters can be created. When more than one filter is used, filters will take the appearance of dropdown selectors.

### Setting up a HubDB for the module

A few columns have specific required IDs to be used by the module. (Labels can be completely customised.)

![][image17]

| Duration is only applicable for video rows, and not necessary to include. |
| :---- |

| Video cards require a FILE-type column with the ID “video”. Non-video cards require a URL-type column with ID “page\_link”. |
| :---- |

## HubDB Video Cards

The HubDB Video Cards module uses a HubDB spreadsheet to control its contents. We use it when we require filtering of cards with the ability to play videos from the cards and pagination.

### Fields

**Selection:**

**Auto:** Automatically pulls rows from the selected HubDB table, with optional filters.

**Manual:** Manually specify row IDs to display.

**Source Table:** Choose the HubDB table containing your video rows.

**Filters:** Add filter groups to restrict which rows are shown (e.g., by category, tag, etc.). Each filter group includes property, operator, and value.

**Order By / Reverse Order:** Specify a column to sort by, and toggle reverse order if needed.

**Row ID:** For manual selection, list the HubDB row IDs to display.

**Sub-filter Options:** Specify column IDs for additional filter dropdowns or buttons.

**Default CTA:** Set the default label for the call-to-action button (e.g., "Watch video").

**CTA Column:** Optionally specify a column to use for custom CTA text per row.

| The CTA column in the HubDB should be a Text column |
| :---- |

**Subheading Column:** Optionally specify a column to display as a subheading in each card.

| The Subheading column in the HubDB should be a Select column |
| :---- |

### Style Fields

**Spacing:** Adjust margin and padding for the module container.

**Stretched Link:** Make the CTA link cover the entire card.

**Card Text Alignment:** Choose left, center, or right alignment for card content.

**Inset Card Body:** Enable to use a colored background for the card body.

**Card Colour / Body Colour / Border Colour:** Set colors for card, body, and border.

**Image Fit / Custom Max Size / Max Width / Max Height:** Control image sizing and fit.

**Play Button:** Show a play button overlay on video thumbnails (light/dark/none).

**CTA Size / Colour / Alignment:** Style the CTA button.

**Equal Heights / Equal Image Heights:** Keep cards and images at consistent heights.

**Image Loading:** Set image loading behavior (lazy/eager/automatic).

**Shadow:** Add a shadow to cards.

**Pagination / Items Per Page:** Enable pagination and set how many cards show per page.

**Responsive Styles:** Set the number of cards per row for desktop, tablet, and mobile.

### HubDB Table Requirements

Your HubDB table should include:

* **name:** The video/card title.  
* **thumbnail:** Image URL for the card.  
* **video:** Video file URL.  
* **description:** Card description.  
* Any additional columns for filtering, subheading, or CTA as needed.

# Functions

## Marketing Modal Engine

The `initCTAModal` function is a lightweight, dependency-safe initialization wrapper built to handle targeted popups using a custom async Bootstrap loading queue. It mimics advanced CTA targeting features (like HubSpot) while granting full control over CSS structure and content. 

### Features

* **Bootstrap 5.1.3 Native:** Works directly with native Bootstrap JS components, events, and focus traps.

* **URL Targeting:** Supports multi-conditional inclusions and exclusions (Contains, Equals, Begins With).

* **Smart Triggers:** Supports Time Delay, Click Action, Scroll Depth, Exit Intent, and Inactivity Idle timers.

* **Frequency Suppression:** Stores dismissals via `localStorage` with a robust fallback to browser cookies for maximum browser compatibility.

* **Campaign & Layout Controls:** Restricts popups to specific date windows and suppresses rendering on responsive screen break sizes.

### Configuration API Reference

```js
initCTAModal({
  modalId: 'string',   // Required. Matches the HTML id attribute of the Bootstrap modal.
  responsive: {},      // Optional. Controls viewport size limits.
  dateRange: {},       // Optional. Restricts execution within date parameters.
  targeting: {},       // Optional. Manages include/exclude page rule matrices.
  trigger: {},         // Optional. Configures user engagement activation logic.
  frequency: {}        // Optional. Determines recurrence suppression.
});
```

1. **`responsive` Object**

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `disableOnSmallScreens` | `Boolean` | `false` | Set to `true` to block execution on small viewports. |
| `breakpoint` | `Number` | `768` | Width threshold (in pixels) beneath which the modal will not fire. |

2. **`dateRange` Object**

| Property | Type | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `start` | `String` | ISO-8601 or standard string format (e.g., `'2026-11-20T00:00:00Z'`). |
| `end` | `String` | ISO-8601 or standard string format (e.g., `'2026-11-30T23:59:59Z'`). |

3. **`targeting` Object**

Accepts arrays containing evaluation objects. For an **Include** rule array, **at least one** condition must match. For an **Exclude** rule array, if **any** condition matches, the engine aborts execution.

| Parameter Option | Type | Rule Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `{ contains: 'value' }` | `String` | Evaluates if string is found anywhere within `window.location.href`. |
| `{ equals: 'value' }` | `String` | Matches `window.location.href` identically. |
| `{ beginsWith: 'value' }` | `String` | Checks if `window.location.href` begins explicitly with the string. |

4. **`trigger` Object**

| `type` | `value` Type | Default | Operational Behavior |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| *(omitted)* | N/A | Immediate | Fires instantly when targeting criteria validate successfully. |
| `'delay'` | `Number` | `0` | Waits designated duration in seconds prior to displaying. |
| `'click'` | `String` | N/A | Binds click event to a CSS selector (e.g., `'.promo-trigger-btn'`). |
| `'scroll'` | `Number` | `50` | Tracks vertical scroll velocity; fires at percentage depth (0-100). |
| `'exit'` | N/A | N/A | Monitors top viewport escape velocity matching desktop exit-intent. |
| `'inactivity'` | `Number` | `30` | Sets an idle countdown (seconds) that resets on mouse, key, or scroll activity. |

5. **`frequency` Object**

| `type` | `value` Type | Operational Behavior |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| *(omitted)* | N/A | Always execute across subsequent page updates if criteria validate. |
| `'session'` | N/A | Suppresses layout visibility after a user dismisses it for the length of that browser tab session. |
| `'never'` | N/A | Absolute restriction after dismissal; the modal will never show again for that user. |
| `'days'` | `Number` | Suppresses execution until specified tracking threshold time has elapsed (e.g., `value: 7`). |

### Troubleshooting & Developer Advice

* **Resetting Persistence State for Local Testing:** Run `localStorage.clear();` or target specific keys natively inside the DevTools Console tab:

  * `localStorage.removeItem('modal_dismissed_YOUR_MODAL_ID');`

* **Storage Key Format:** Keys automatically group inside browser application panels under the identifier format syntax string: `modal_dismissed_{modalId}`.

* **Framework Precedence:** If you pass a trigger type of `'click'`, the target trigger element must exist in the DOM at the time `initCTAModal()` runs. If elements load dynamically later, initialize the modal wrapper after rendering the template nodes.
